I really wanted to like this game but it wasn't for me, here is a review saying why:

Stardew Valley is a game based mainly on the concept of farming or in general producing resources considering you can also mine, forage, and do things such as chop trees but there is also a energy bar/hunger bar that drains the more you use items such as a pickaxe, axe, weapon, walking in general, and even watering a crop takes energy. Now lets get it straight that tons of games have a hunger/energy bar and are still good games but in them food can be obtained much more easily but in Stardew Valley your energy bar is made to have around 250 max energy but each action such and using most tools use up around 2 energy but that is for each time you simply swing an axe, pickaxe, hoe, etc. but to chop down a tree and remove the stump that would take around 12 swings draining a lot of energy from your bar. How the mines work is that you mine rocks placed around the rooms you uncover and that to proceed through the mines you have to mine a certain rock that will have a staircase under it but that can take awhile to find and that drains some of your energy bar unless your lucky enough to find the staircase earlier.
The NPCs are lifeless and make me feel like I'm a drone walking around town staring at them as they tell me something that probably won't matter at all and I can't really ask them a question or bring up any conversation. There are cutseens but I seem to find myself trying to find every single cutseen in the game and that I don't have much of an affect on what happens other than saying something to change what someone says in a cutseen then realizing that the cutseen won't really be referred to later in the game.
Every time I make some money I feel like it's not worth the effort. I also think that each season should be as long as an in game year because it takes around half a season for a crop to grow and that at the end of each season your crops will die and you'll have to buy ones that are in season but each successful harvest gets me less than 700 gold. When I first got this game I found it boring shortly but I kept playing because I thought there would be some sort of magic and I played thinking that the magic was just around the corner and that when the magic came the game would suddenly be fun and amazing but after my first in game year I realized there was no magic and that I just hated the game and found it boring. 
EDIT: This review might be a bit tilted and inaccurate in some places so make sure to read more reviews.

Stardew Valley est un cozy-game 2D en vue du dessus. Dans ce jeu, vous incarnez un personnage qui démenage en campagne pour devenir fermier parce qu'il en avait marre de la vie de bureau. C'est donc un simulateur de vie où vous pourrez créer des amitiés voire même vous marier.

Le jeu possède plusieurs activités que vous pouvez réaliser pour passer le temps comme l'agriculture, la pêche ou l'extraction minière. Cependant, je trouve très difficile de faire une grosse session de jeu car c'est pas si intéressant à long terme.

Le jeu peut être jugé intéressant pour son aspect social. Il y'a de mémoire 28 PNJ dans la petite commune où vous vivez et vous pouvez parler avec chacun d'eux. Ils possèdent chacun leurs propres personnalités et vous pouvez leurs offrir des cadeaux pour monter dans leur estime et devenir amis avec eux. Je trouve personnellement cet aspect du jeu inintéressant, on passe notre temps à essayer d'offrir des cadeaux à chaque personnage en fonction de leurs préferences. Contrairement à ce que l'on pourrait penser, on n'a pas de réel dialogue avec les personnages, on ne peut pas choisir quoi leur dire ou de quoi parle. Limitant fortement les interactions disponibles.

En conclusion, je pense clairement que ce jeu n'est pas fait pour moi. J'ai trouvé la boucle de gameplay inintéressante et ennuyante (C'est à dire une des activités + parler et offrir aux PNJ). Il y a des tentatives de redynamiser le gameplay, notamment avec les évènements mais ils sauvent à peine les meubles. Je ne prends aucun plaisir à jouer au jeu mais si la description que j'ai faites vous intéresse, vous pouvez toujours tenter.

reviews.review:
​Stardew Valley is, at its core, a masterpiece of the cozy-farming genre. Whether you’re meticulously planning your crop rotations, delving into the mines, or wooing the local villagers, the game offers a level of charm and depth that is rarely matched. It shines brightest when played with a partner or friends—sharing the workload of a growing farm makes the experience feel truly collaborative and rewarding.
​The Breaking Point: "Connecting to Online Services..."
However, the current technical state of the game has made it nearly impossible to recommend for those looking for that specific multiplayer magic. Recently, many players (myself included) have hit a literal brick wall: the co-op menu often hangs indefinitely on the message "connecting to online services." This isn't just a minor lag spike; it’s a total service failure that prevents the multiplayer menu from even loading, effectively stripping away the game’s best feature. While the single-player experience remains intact, the lack of a reliable fix for these server-side handshake issues makes the "Co-op" button feel like a decorative ornament rather than a functional feature.

I see the Steam charts. I see the millions of human hours wasted in this colorful purgatory. Stardew Valley is not a game: It is a chemical pacifier for those who find the friction of a real challenge - like Dark Souls or Factorio - too taxing for their limited bandwidth. 

You start with a gift from a dead grandfather. That’s the first red flag. In a true Meritocracy, you start with nothing and earn the right to exist. Here, you are handed a life because you "felt sad" in a corporate office. 

The issues with the game:
- You can’t lose. You can’t go bankrupt. Even if you pass out in the mines because you failed to manage your energy bar - honestly a rudimentary variable that even a toddler could track - someone just carries you home. There is no consequence. A world without consequence is a world without Truth. 

- In Stardew, you "win" over NPCs by feeding them their favorite items like trained seals. It’s not social intelligence, it’s a repetitive fetch-quest that masquerades as human connection. If you spend 100 hours trying to marry a pixelated alcoholic named Shane, you aren't "gaming". You are coping. 

- The game carries an illusion of productivity: Casual players claim they like the "grind." Let’s be clear: Clicking on a parsnip two hundred times is not a grind. Optimizing a 12-way intersection in Factorio under the threat of a Biter evolution is a grind. Stardew is just a chore-simulator for the unambitious. 

Ironically, the "villain" of the game - JojaMart - is the only entity that follows a semblance of logic. They offer efficiency, standardized pricing, and a clear path to progress through capital. Yet, the game expects me to spend my time collecting "bundles" for magical forest spirits (Junimos) to fix a community center? I don't play games to fix communities. I play games to dominate game mechanics.

Final Assessment: If Stardew Valley is in your "Most Played" list, you've accepted your role as a package tourist. You're still at the base of the mountain watering plants, meanwhile Real Gamers such as myself have already reached the summit sipping on a glass of wine. Be better than this.
